review.summary: Phase 20's prepublication qualification is genuine, executed, and mechanically bound to the exact reviewed source 519219d6 at commit 0716cfd. I re-derived commands_for(20) from tools/check_phase.py:70-108 (commands_for(17)+commands_for(19), renamed/de-duplicated, plus generate_models --verify-fixtures and both check-native-exports runs) and counted exactly 59 — matching docs/CI.md:154 and the 59 records in docs/reviews/phase-20-attempt-03.checks.json, all exit_code 0, zero timeouts, source_unchanged true, source_sha256 equal to the reviewed source and the same 09:02:24 snapshot as docs/checks/phase-20.json; tools/review_phase.py:187 enforces ordered list equality, so the set cannot be trimmed. ci_commands_for(20) yields exactly 41, matching docs/CI.md:162 and the 48+1=49 matrix at .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:90-91 (including red-team-json-unification on both compilers), and tools/test_ci.py:111-145 asserts those counts against the live workflow and command functions rather than prose. Both clean archive proofs record requireClean true / effectiveDirty false at releaseCommit 0716cfd with identical file inventories (1.89.0 13ebff0d, 1.99.0 c908cad8), and scripts/check-access-release.py ran in-gate at exit 0, re-hashing both retained archives, requiring releaseCommit == HEAD, comparing every packaged byte against both the working tree and `git show <commit>`, asserting inventory equality in both directions, and requiring all four offline examples plus three external consumer runs for 0.2.2 (scripts/check-access-release.py:33-47). The shipped fix is real: validation.rs:1209-1229 resolves and validates regex/bound metadata before relaxing only the eight named string formats and requestOnly string bounds in response modes, leaves unknown kinds failing closed at line 1241, and keeps Mode::Request strict; examples/response_compatibility.rs reproduces the reported defects byte-exactly (job-1/p-1/map-1, "2026-01-05 00:00:00", offsetless timestamps, FUTURE_* vocabulary, nested unknown data, u64::MAX projection fallback) while retaining the three disputed structural rejections, and it executes from the extracted archive and from a separate consumer crate on both compilers. Independent regression evidence is substantial (g25_fixtures 15,658 mutations/46 roots/55 projection fields, g25-oracle 15,658 independent outcomes, corpus-hash-bound tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:62-141). The live rerun is mechanically rebound to current runtime inputs (tools/live_evidence.py:266 requires runtimeInputsSha256 == runtime_fingerprint(); gate output reports 17 verified / 22 observed / not_needed) and the 403/400 outcomes are reported without inflation. Both medium findings from attempt 02 are now genuinely closed: tools/release_delivery.py:127-138 requires actual phase-20 registry_publication metadata matching the registry receipt, and scripts/verify-publication.py:56-71,249-252 refuses to fetch or write a 0.2.2 receipt without an accepted current-source readiness review and re-checks it before writing, each with hermetic negative tests (tools/test_release_delivery.py:258-339). Publication, the v0.2.2 tag and terminal 49-job CI remain pending delivery obligations by construction, and no receipt is fabricated anywhere. Remaining deficiencies are low: the activated current-version document guard is still invoked only by a mandated manual tools/test_ci.py run rather than by the delivery guard; verify-publication's --delta path keeps a G10-specific allowed-change list reachable with --version 0.2.2; the qualification chunk record mixes superseded acceptance fields with its pending status; and the packaged README links repository-relative receipt paths that do not exist yet. No blocker or high finding. 46/50.

findings.description: verify_publication_metadata now requires phases[20].registry_publication with status published_and_verified, the canonical evidence path and the registry receipt's source_commit, which closes attempt 02's medium finding. What remains unenforced is the current-version release-document guard itself: tools/test_ci.py:328-349 selects publications[-1] and returns at line 347 while the workspace version (0.2.2) differs from the latest recorded publication (0.2.1), so the receipt-link assertions in README.md:40-42, CHANGELOG.md:6-8, docs/RELEASE.md:5-7 and docs/STABILITY.md:4-5 are inert today. Activation depends on the manual obligation recorded in docs/phase-status.json:4574 (create registry_publication, then run tools/test_ci.py and preserve its output), and docs/phase-status.json:4533 deliberately preserves the frozen 59-command snapshot rather than re-running the HEAD-bound candidate checker after receipt-only delivery commits. The practical risk is small (the CHANGELOG link format at CHANGELOG.md:6 already matches the assertion at tools/test_ci.py:366, and validate_receipts independently verifies the receipt's identity, ownership, checksum, files, vcs, tag and CI), but at the moment it matters the guard is procedural rather than mechanical.
findings.required_fix: In the next qualified source change, have tools/release_delivery.verify assert directly that the release documents link the canonical receipt (for example require '](' + registry_path + ')' in CHANGELOG.md and README.md, or invoke the test_ci guard), with a negative test in tools/test_release_delivery.py, so delivery cannot pass while the current-version document guard is skipped.

findings.description: check_delta() hardcodes the 0.1.0 baseline receipt, the cached .local/artifacts/scm-sdk-0.1.0-registry.crate path and an allowed-change set limited to the reviewed G10 delta, but main() routes any --version into it. Running the documented tool with --version 0.2.2 --delta would read docs/checks/release-registry-0.1.0.json, compare a 0.2.2 archive against the 0.1.0 package and fail with 'Unexpected packaged change outside the reviewed G10 delta', which is fail-closed but misleading for this release line.
findings.required_fix: Gate the --delta mode to the versions it was reviewed for (for example reject --delta unless args.version is the G10 patch, or parameterize baselineVersion and the allowed-change set), and cover the rejection in tools/test_release_022.py.

findings.description: The qualification-and-package chunk record carries status 'pending_fresh_source_review' alongside accepted_total 45, accepted_categories, accepted_review and review_decision 'accepted' bound to the superseded source ee60edd5, plus an unexplained historical_accepted_total 44. Its attempts field is a list of review paths, whereas the phase-19 chunks at docs/phase-status.json:3906-4032 record attempt objects with totals and accepted flags. Nothing is misstated (accepted_source_sha256 discloses the older source and tools/review_phase.py:305-320 will reject a non-attempt-five chunk whose source differs), but the mixed vocabulary makes it easy to misread the chunk as currently accepted.
findings.required_fix: Rename the superseded fields to a historical_* group (or nest them under a superseded_acceptance object) while the chunk awaits its current-source review, and align the attempts schema with the phase-19 chunk records so totals and decisions are machine-readable for both phases.

findings.description: The packaged README (sha 5baf828a, part of both archive proofs) links docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.2.json and docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.2.json, which do not exist yet, and the archive ships no docs/ directory (scripts/check-package.py:43-45), so those relative links cannot resolve from the registry page even after the receipts are committed. The conditional wording at README.md:40-42 and docs/RELEASE.md:7 correctly prevents any false publication claim, and this matches the pattern of the already published 0.1.1/0.2.0/0.2.1 READMEs, so it is a discoverability nit rather than an accuracy defect.
findings.required_fix: For publication-critical receipt references in the packaged README, use absolute repository URLs (as already done for the crates.io links at README.md:27-33) in a future qualified source change, so readers of the registry page can reach the evidence.

Registry publication, the v0.2.2 tag and the terminal exact 49-job CI run have not happened. docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.2.json, docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.2.json and a phase-20 remote-CI receipt do not exist, phase 20 has no delivery or registry_publication entry, and tools/release_delivery.verify therefore cannot yet run. These are pending obligations, not completed outcomes.

This record is a prepublication readiness assessment and cannot advance phase 20. The qualification-and-package chunk is accepted only at the superseded source ee60edd5 (attempt 2 of 5, status pending_fresh_source_review) and registry-and-remote-delivery has no attempts; both require their own current-source acceptance, and a fresh complete-phase review after delivery is still required.
Receipt integrity is digest-based and assumes a trusted repository writer; no execution receipt is cryptographically authenticated, as docs/PHASES.md and tools/release_delivery.py:1-7 state.

Live acceptance remains partial and unexplained in part: three Red Team reads returned 403 and IAM scope creation and Gateway provisioning returned 400 with the cause unestablished and an SDK request-shape defect not excluded; those methods stay live-unqualified, no mutation/cleanup chain was completed, and the same outcomes were observed for 0.2.1.
The reported airs-cli-rs loopback failures could not be reproduced or refuted here (the consumer checkout is unreachable from this host), and no consumer adoption is claimed.

Generated projection-field rustdoc and broader unpaired-root pairing diagnostics are explicitly deferred and not delivered in this patch; retained vendor numeric/array domains can still reject an unexpected out-of-domain response for operations without a TypeScript counterpart.
